nodes.description: In utero exposure to certain antiepileptic drugs, particularly valproate and phenytoin/topiramate, increases the risk of orofacial clefting.

evidence.reference_title: Valproic acid monotherapy in pregnancy and major congenital malformations.
evidence.snippet: The use of valproic acid monotherapy in the first trimester was associated with significantly increased risks of several congenital malformations, as compared with no use of antiepileptic drugs or with use of other antiepileptic drugs.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in BMP4 are associated with subepithelial, microform, and overt cleft lip.
evidence.snippet: We identified missense and nonsense mutations in the BMP4 gene in 1 of 30 cases of microform clefts, 2 of 87 cases with subepithelial defects in the orbicularis oris muscle (OOM), 5 of 968 cases of overt CL/P, and 0 of 529 controls.

nodes.description: Lip and palate morphogenesis is governed by a conserved gene regulatory network in which transcription factors and signaling pathways (IRF6-GRHL3 in the periderm/oral epithelium; SHH, BMP4, FGF, and WNT signaling; MSX1, FOXE1, PAX7, TP63) coordinate epithelial-mesenchymal interactions. Pathogenic variants and common risk alleles at these loci perturb the network, reducing the developmental robustness of fusion and increasing cleft susceptibility. IRF6 is the single most important locus, contributing to both syndromic (Van der Woude) and nonsyndromic clefting.
nodes.id: Disruption of the Orofacial Developmental Gene Regulatory Network

nodes.description: During weeks 4-7 of development, cranial neural crest-derived mesenchyme populates the frontonasal prominence and paired maxillary prominences. Formation of the upper lip and primary palate requires the medial nasal prominences to merge with each other and with the maxillary prominences. Deficient neural crest cell migration, proliferation, or survival, or failure of epithelial seam breakdown at the sites of contact, prevents fusion and produces a cleft of the lip (with or without the alveolus), which may be unilateral or bilateral.
nodes.id: Failure of Lip and Primary Palate Fusion

evidence.reference_title: Cleft lip and palate: understanding genetic and environmental influences.
evidence.snippet: The common forms of CLP involve disruption of tissue planes above the lip extending into the nares and/or the palate (hard and/or soft)

nodes.description: Between weeks 6 and 9, the paired secondary palatal shelves grow vertically beside the tongue, elevate to a horizontal position above the descending tongue, grow toward the midline, and fuse. Fusion requires apposition of the medial edge epithelia, formation of a midline epithelial seam, and subsequent removal of the seam by epithelial apoptosis and/or epithelial-mesenchymal transition, allowing mesenchymal confluence. Disruption of shelf growth, delayed or failed elevation, impaired seam formation, or persistence of the medial edge epithelium yields a cleft of the secondary palate.

evidence.snippet: the embryonic primary and secondary palatal shelves develop as outgrowths from the medial nasal and maxillary prominences, respectively, remodel and fuse to form the intact roof of the oral cavity.

evidence.reference_title: Transforming growth factor-beta 3 is required for secondary palate fusion.
evidence.snippet: The defect appears to result from impaired adhesion of the apposing medial edge epithelia of the palatal shelves and subsequent elimination of the mid-line epithelial seam.

evidence.reference_title: Tobacco smoking and oral clefts: a meta-analysis.
evidence.snippet: Consistent, moderate and statistically significant associations were found between maternal smoking and cleft lip, with or without cleft palate (relative risk 1.34, 95% confidence interval 1.25-1.44) and between maternal smoking and cleft palate (relative risk 1.22, 95% confidence interval 1.10-1.35).

nodes.description: Heterozygous loss-of-function variants in the homeobox transcription factor genes MSX1 and DLX4 reduce the dose of a sequence-specific transcriptional regulator expressed in the craniofacial mesenchyme. For DLX4 the founding frameshift allele failed to activate Dlx regulatory elements in a reporter assay, implying haploinsufficiency, and Dlx4 is expressed in the murine palatal shelf mesenchyme before palate closure. Reduced dose of these regulators is placed upstream of both lip and secondary palate fusion failure.

evidence.reference_title: DLX4 is associated with orofacial clefting and abnormal jaw development.
evidence.snippet: Wild-type human DLX4, but not mutant DLX4_c.546delG, could activate two murine Dlx conserved regulatory elements, implying that the mutation caused haploinsufficiency.

evidence.reference_title: Complete sequencing shows a role for MSX1 in non-syndromic cleft lip and palate.
evidence.snippet: Five different missense mutations in seven unrelated subjects with clefting are described.

nodes.description: Micromachined 96-well microplate in which an epithelium is overlaid onto an extracellular matrix-embedded mesenchyme. SHH from the epithelium sets up a gradient of SHH-driven transcription in the mesenchyme, and small-molecule inhibitors of SHH secretion, matrix transport and mesenchymal sensing antagonize it. Cells are human fetal oral epithelial GMSM-K (SHH-null and SHH-overexpressing variants), mouse embryonic 3T3 Shh-Light2 mesenchyme and mouse cranial neural crest O9-1 mesenchyme.

Rare BMP4 missense and nonsense variants are associated with a cleft lip spectrum that extends from overt cleft lip to microform clefts and subepithelial defects of the orbicularis oris muscle. The functional effect of the individual variants on BMP4 signaling was not established in the source; reduced BMP4 ligand activity is the inferred mechanism, and the authors also raise a role for BMP4 in wound healing.

nodes.description: SUMO1 haploinsufficiency lowers the supply of the SUMO1 protein tag. The products of several cleft genes are sumoylated, and a Sumo1 hypomorphic allele interacts genetically with a loss-of-function allele at one of those loci, so reduced sumoylation is proposed to weaken a network of palatogenesis regulators. The human evidence is a single patient.

evidence.reference_title: SUMO1 haploinsufficiency leads to cleft lip and palate.
evidence.snippet: We studied a patient with isolated cleft lip and palate and a balanced chromosomal translocation that disrupts the SUMO1 (small ubiquitin-related modifier) gene, resulting in haploinsufficiency.

evidence.reference_title: SUMO1 haploinsufficiency leads to cleft lip and palate.
evidence.snippet: Products of several genes implicated in clefting are sumoylated, and the Sumo1 hypomorphic allele interacts genetically with a loss-of-function allele for one of these loci.
